_comment: PUBLIC section -> price band map, from the official Sharks 2026-27 full-season seating chart (public marketing material). Band prices are the team's own published per-game averages. Nothing here identifies a seat: it is the whole building's price structure, and no band is marked as ours. See ops#19.
_why: This is the team's own definition of which seats are EQUIVALENT - the baseline comp set for ops#11, replacing a geometric guess. It also lets the app place a seat in the building's price structure with no scraping at all.

_transcriptionStatus.sectionAssignment: NOT TRANSCRIBED - and the shape is now known to be wrong. An automated colour extraction from the chart reached only ~65% self-consistency against the mirror check (7/11 lower and 7/13 upper pairs), failing through rays straying across wedge boundaries. Deliberately NOT committed; a plausible-but-wrong section map is worse than none. See _modelCorrection.
_transcriptionStatus._blocker: Section-to-band assignment must be read off the chart's colour coding, and the chart is not in this repo. Guessing it is exactly the failure mode ops#19 warns about, and the same one that made the hand-transcribed tier table need its own validator. Left empty on purpose; scripts/check_price_bands.py reports the gap loudly rather than passing on absent data.
_transcriptionStatus._confidence: The band prices below are TRANSCRIBED, not measured. They are checked for internal consistency by the validator, not against an external source.

_priceNote: avgPerGame is the published full-season average per game. `renew` is the renewal rate, `new` the new-buyer rate. Some bands publish only one of the two; absent means not published, not zero.
_rowScopeNote: Most bands are section-level: a section belongs to exactly one band. Promenade Row 1 is NOT - it is row 1 *inside* promenade sections, priced separately from the rows behind it. So the map is really (section, rowScope) -> band, and the coverage check groups by rowScope. Missing this makes 'every section assigned exactly once' unsatisfiable and would push someone toward deleting the check instead of fixing the model.
_ringsNote: Section labels around each seating level, starting from centre ice on the Sharks-bench side. Order is COUNTER-clockwise on screen (101 -> 128 -> 127 ...): an earlier note called it clockwise, which was wrong - with screen y increasing downward, clockwise from the bottom runs toward 102, not 128. Direction does not affect the contiguity or symmetry checks, which are direction-agnostic, but the label should not lie. Transcribed from Ticketmaster's public static seatmap and independently confirmed against the SAP Center venue map Wesley supplied - both show the same 22 lower sections with the same six gaps. Corroborated further by the mirror-symmetry check in scripts/check_price_bands.py.
_familyNote: `family` groups bands that form one published price ladder, and `rank` 1 is the most expensive. The lower / promenade / upper / club ladders are named as such on the chart. The 'premium' family (Glass, Teal, Orange) is NOT - those are product names, and grouping them into a ranked ladder is an INFERENCE from their prices. It buys a real ordering check; if the chart shows they are unrelated products, split them into separate families rather than weakening the check.
_ringsOpenQuestion: The band names in this file (Promenade 1-3, Promenade Row 1, Upper Attack 1-2, Upper Goal 1-2, Club 1-5, Glass, Teal, Orange) do NOT map onto the 100/200/PL section numbering visible on Ticketmaster's map. Ticketmaster shows two rings plus nine PL sections; the Sharks' chart implies at least four priced levels. So the level names cannot be matched to rings by inference - that mapping has to come from the Sharks' own colour-coded chart. Do not guess it. See ops#19.

_modelCorrection.finding: bands are ROW RANGES WITHIN sections, not whole sections
_modelCorrection.evidence: Radial pixel scans of the official 2026-27 Sharks365 chart. Section 115, from the ice outward: CLUB 2 (~70px of rows) then LOWER 1 CENTER (~38px). Then the 200 level: PROMENADE ROW 1 CENTER as a single ~4px strip, then PROMENADE 1, then PROMENADE 2. Section 101 likewise: CLUB 3, CLUB 2, LOWER 1 CENTER, then PROMENADE 1/2.
_modelCorrection.consequence: The `sections` array on each band is the WRONG SHAPE. The real key is (section, rowFrom, rowTo). A section-only map cannot answer 'which seats are equivalent to mine', which is what ops#11 needs it for, because two seats in the same section can be in different bands.
_modelCorrection.whatTheChartCannotGive: ROW NUMBERS. The chart draws row bands but prints no row numbers, so the boundaries are visible as pixels and not as data. Row ranges need a different source - most likely a per-seat price lookup in Account Manager, or the member invoice, which prices the seats actually held.

_endAsymmetry.finding: the two ends of the rink are priced DIFFERENTLY, so the arena is not left-right symmetric
_endAsymmetry.evidence: The chart labels one end 'SHARKS ATTACK TWICE'. That end carries UPPER ATTACK 1/2; the other carries UPPER GOAL 1/2, at different prices ($58/$37 vs $54/$34 renew). Confirmed empirically: scoring extracted band stacks against a left-right mirror gave 0/10 agreement, while scoring against the LONG axis (top-bottom, 101<->115) gave 7/11.
_endAsymmetry.consequence: The placement checks in scripts/check_price_bands.py assume the wrong symmetry. `expectedArcs: 2` plus equal-length arcs encodes left-right mirroring, which would have REJECTED correct data for every Attack/Goal band - those occupy one end only and so form a single arc. A false alarm from the very check written to prevent false confidence. Not repaired here: the model shape is changing to (section, row) anyway, so the arc checks need rework rather than patching.
